messages:
rachel: Heads-up — we need to cut release/1.16 before tomorrow morning cutoff. I can create the branch but want to confirm backport rules and changelog process. Who's around to help with quick triage?
jon: I can hop on. What time is cutoff?
rachel: Cutoff is 08:00 UTC tomorrow. Prefer branch created a few hours before so teams can finish last-minute cherrypicks.
mitch: Quick Q: do we still require a signed-off changelog entry for any PR that touches public API?
tara: Yes — API-affecting PRs need an entry in CHANGELOG.md in the release PR or a linked changelog issue. If it's minor doc/typo, tag it as non-user-facing.achel: Great. Also, for backports: we follow the existing policy — label PRs with backport-request and target release/* branch. But should we allow high-risk backports during this window?
jon: No, high-risk (behavioral changes, schema bumps) should be deferred unless a customer-blocking bug. Low-risk fixes ok. If uncertain, ping eng-sre for signoff.
mitch: For the branch creation itself, use this command:
```
# from main
git fetch origin
git checkout -b release/1.16 origin/main
# push upstream
git push origin release/1.16
```
I'll run the create-release script if someone wants me to.
rachel: @mitch please run the script at T-3h. Add a post with the branch ref and link to the release PR.
mitch: On it.
sam: For cherry-pick requests, please add a short rationale and risk assessment in the PR body and add the label `backport-request`. That speeds triage.
tara: Also: use the changelog template in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/changelog.md — keeps things consistent.
jon: Can we set an automated blocker for merges into main after cutoff? Maybe a branch protection or gate?
mitch: We have a deploy-bot check we can flip to strict. @deploy-bot can you post current cutoff gate rules?
deploy-bot: Current policy: merges to main are allowed but protected by `release-freeze` check which will be set to required 1 hour before cutoff. Maintainers can override with `release-emergency` tag.
rachel: OK — sounds good. One more ops ask: if you create a backport PR, please ping this thread with the PR url and label so we can queue it. Short messages are fine.
jon: If a reviewer spots a changelog missing, mark `needs-changelog` and assign to author.
sam: I made a tiny checklist we can reuse: 1) branch created, 2) release PR opened, 3) changelog entries collected, 4) backport queue triaged, 5) deploy-bot freeze enabled. I can paste it in the release issue after branch creation.
mitch: Branch created: `release/1.16` -> https://git.example.com/redwood/repo/compare/release/1.16 (follow-up: opened release PR #1420).
rachel: Thanks! I'll start reviewing queued backports. Please keep notes short here with PR links.
jon: Backport PR #1423 for `fix/kv-cache-off-by-one` opened, labelled `backport-request`, risk: low, changelog: Added entry.
tara: Reviewing #1423 now.
jon: Small heads-up — I'm going to hold any refactor backports unless they are trivial.
sam: Reminder: if you need a canary deploy on dedicated to verify a backport, file a `canary-request` in infra and tag `release/1.16`.
mitch: Also, anyone doing a security fix: mark `security` and ping sec. We treat those as emergency eligible.
rachel: Last call: cutoff in 2 hours. If you have pending backports, tag them now or they won't make the release. :alarm_clock: :eyes:
jon: Tagging #1425 (performance) and #1426 (docs).
tara: #1425 looks fine, merging after CI. #1426 is doc-only.
mitch: Enabling `release-freeze` check now.
deploy-bot: `release-freeze` set to required by @mitch at 2150010200. Overrides require `release-emergency` label.
rachel: Awesome — thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a short summary in the release issue. 👍
jon: Thanks — will monitor CI and poke reviewers as needed.
sam: Copy — I'll post the checklist in the release issue and keep an eye on backport queue.
